annotations.text:
THE RETHINK

The old dashboard showed measured facts, a 10x-wrong model and an unsupported thesis at equal visual weight. That was the real failure — not the layout.

New rule: a figure reaches the front page only if it can be scored against something that actually gets reported. Everything else is demoted to a driver, or to evidence, or cut.

Four panels are cut outright.

WIREFRAMES, DELIBERATELY UGLY

Greyscale and hand-lettered so you judge structure without style getting a vote.

The load-bearing move is the track record sitting directly under the estimate. On day one it reads "0 quarters scored" — and saying that loudly is the whole design thesis. A number with no record should look like one.

ASSUMPTIONS BECOME INPUTS

The catalogue-share constant that made the old royalty model 10x too big was buried in a file. Here every assumption is a control with your name on it, and the sensitivity panel says which one actually matters.

One assumption carries ~13% of the answer. That is the number to argue about.

THREE VISUAL LANGUAGES, ONE SCREEN

Same data, same structure, so the comparison is fair. All three drop the dark-slate / Inter / rounded-card system entirely.

A · BROADSHEET — warm paper, serif numerals, rules instead of cards. Reads like a research note you would publish. Most legible; least "dashboard".

Main holds A as the leading candidate.

B · INSTRUMENT

Near-black, monospace throughout, hairline rules, amber for anything you own. Every figure on one screen, no scrolling.

For: density, and reading across both names at once.
Against: unwelcoming unless you are in it daily, and it flattens the difference between a measured number and an assumption.

C · BLUEPRINT

Technical drawing. Visible grid, dimension lines marking quarter-elapsed, revision number in the title block, and a NOT VERIFIED stamp where the track record should be.

The stamp is the point: a provisional drawing looks provisional. Strongest fit for the epistemics — riskiest if it reads as a gimmick.

LEVEL 2 — THE CHARTS AND TABLES YOU ALREADY HAVE

Restyled into the leading theme so the product reads as one thing rather than two. Same data, same statistics — control limits, slicers, quarter comparison — but positioned as how you CHECK a driver, not what you open the product for.

If you pick theme B or C instead, these follow it.

THE TABLE EARNS ITS PLACE BY BEING HONEST

Real rows, and they show the texture: subscriber deltas of 0 / 10,000 / 0 / 102,000 down the column, because YouTube quantises to the nearest thousand.

Drag the range before 16 Feb 2026 and channel counts read n/a, never 0.

A HARDER LIMIT THAN I FIRST THOUGHT

The legacy aggregate never recorded video counts, so releases before 2026 are n/a — not comparable at all, rather than comparable-with-caveats like views.

2026 Q1 is flagged mixed: its 3,812 releases are the first per-channel reading, not a release burst.

The correlation grid ends up here as a footnote — 3 of 90 against 4.5 expected.

EVERY REMAINING SURFACE, IN BROADSHEET

The app now has one visual language end to end. Level 1 is the driver tree; the rest are Level 2 evidence plus the one unauthenticated screen.

The sensitivity panel on Drivers is the point of the whole level: the MEASURED input moves the answer least (±₹7cr), and the two assumptions you set move it most (±₹31cr and ±₹19cr). That is the honest shape of this model.

CONCENTRATION IS THE UNHEDGED RISK

64% of Tips' 30-day reach sits on ONE channel; Saregama's largest is 39%. A single algorithm change moves two thirds of one estimate.

That belongs on a page, not buried in a channel table — so Channels leads with it rather than with a leaderboard.

REAL PRICES THIS TIME

TIPS ₹648.05 (−1.81%), SAREGAMA ₹492.80 (+1.09%), close 28 Aug. My earlier Overview mockup used ₹832.40 and ₹604.15 — illustrative and wrong; these are from fct_adjusted_price_daily.

The share-price screen deliberately draws NO line between reach and price. It is context for your judgement, nothing more.
